failure_summary.description: Added unsupported properties or weakened exact quantitative conclusions by substituting a familiar, more generic formulation.
Misread the branching-process regime at and above the threshold, overlooking the stated conditioning and inclusive endpoint.
Chose an incompatible pair of probability bounds without checking how their rates compare as the parameter tends to its limit.
Missed the exact uniqueness claim required for a complete characterization of the minimizers.

patch.reasoning: The recurring issue is selecting an attractive or familiar formulation without establishing every clause, endpoint, and quantitative detail. Focused checks should prevent unsupported strengthenings, preserve the exact model and quantifiers, and distinguish precise bounds from conventional definitions.

edits.content:
## Strongest Valid Means Strongest Proved
For each option, treat every added property as a separate obligation: structural claims, least-energy conclusions, multiplicative compatibility, uniqueness, and stronger extremum conditions all require explicit support. First establish which options are true; only then select the strongest among them. Do not infer an extra conclusion merely because it sounds like a natural strengthening.

## Compare Quantitative Claims Literally
Do not silently add or remove constants in an estimate because one form is more conventional. Compare the stated rates in the relevant limiting regime, and check that lower and upper bounds can hold simultaneously. When powers or logarithms differ, test their relative sizes rather than relying on an intuitive ranking.

## Preserve the Exact Framework and Scope
Do not transfer a familiar theorem unchanged to a nonstandard derivative, a conditioned sampling law, or a specialized invariant unless its definitions and hypotheses match. Track conditioning and threshold endpoints exactly (`<`, `=`, `≥`); for classification questions, distinguish existence from uniqueness and check whether the claim concerns one minimizer or all minimizers.
